transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
Early voting this year has outpaced numbers from the last midterm elections in 2022.
As NPR's Hansi Luong reports, more than 49 million ballots have already been cast with
less than three days left until Tuesday's Election Day.
Around the country, voters have returned more than 22 million mail-in ballots as of Friday.
They've also cast more than 26 million ballots in person at early voting sites.
That's according to statistics compiled by the University of Florida's Election Lab.
And altogether, that's higher than the total early voting numbers for the 2022 midterms.
This year's numbers are expected to taper off, as some states end early in-person voting
before Election Day.
For mail-in voters who haven't returned their ballots yet, it is likely too late now for
the U.S. Postal Service to deliver them in time for them to be received by Election Day.
Voters can consider returning their mail-in ballot at their local election office or any
available ballot drop box instead.
Hansi Luong, NPR News.
Campaigning continues in Michigan, where the contest for U.S. Senate remains a toss-up.
As NPR's Sam Greenglass tells us, the race is significant.
A win in Michigan could mean control of the Senate as well.
It has been 30 years since Michigan last sent a Republican to the Senate and Trump's approval
rating is abysmal in Michigan now.
And yet, polls suggest this race is a toss-up.
Democrats are testing a nominee pretty far left on the spectrum, Abdul El-Sayed.
He's an epidemiologist harnessing anger at the political establishment and betting he
can beat Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers by galvanizing young voters, disenfranchised
voters, even former Trump voters.
That's NPR's Sam Greenglass.
The Republican National Committee says President Trump is changing his schedule this weekend
to rally Republicans in two states with critical Senate races.
He'll visit Selena, Kansas, and Dubuque, Iowa on Sunday for back-to-back rallies.
The changes underscore the Republican Party's last-minute push to turn out voters for the
midterm elections.
As gasoline remains $1.20 higher than a year ago and as diesel hovers, around $6.30, major
oil companies Exxon, Mobil, Chevron, and Shell report soaring profits this quarter.
NPR's Willa Rubin listened to the company's earnings calls.
Exxon doubled its earnings compared to this time last year.
Shell's earnings nearly doubled.
Chevron's were up 180 percent.
Together, the company's earned just over $36 billion this quarter.
All kinds of oil products have gotten pricier this year.
Due to the war in Iran, less oil has been getting out of the Middle East, and Ukraine's
attacks on Russian refineries have especially hampered the global diesel supply.
The oil companies gave some of their earnings to shareholders through dividends, but for
the most part, they're in a wait-and-see stance.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News from Cleveland.
China has conducted military drills in a contested area between Beijing and the Philippines.
The drills took place just days after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth vowed to deter any aggression
in the region.
Yan Carmen's in Brumby has more from Taipei.
China's military says the patrols were in "response to the Philippines' rights violations
and provocative acts" and involved naval and air forces seeking to enhance their control
of the region.
Manila and Beijing, who claims much of the South China Sea, have repeatedly clashed over
their contesting claims in the waters.
A 2016 ruling by an international tribunal in The Hague rejected almost all of Beijing's
maritime claims to the region.
China's maneuvers came just days after Defense Secretary Hegseth vowed the U.S. would deter
coercion and aggression in the region, and pledged additional funding for defense cooperation
with the Philippines.
For NPR News, I'm Yan Carmen's in Brumby, in Taipei.
The sell-off of tech stocks continued on Wall Street Friday, with traders worried that a
frenzy around AI sent the stocks too high.
Israel saw its biggest loss since 1974.
The S&P 500 dropped 1.8 percent for its worst day since June.
The NASDAQ composite finished down 2.9 percent, the Dow Jones industrial average off 1.1 percent.
Christa Pike says she's in constant pain since surviving an attempt at lethal injection
in a Tennessee prison last month.
She issued her first public statement Friday, expressing gratitude for the support she's
received.
She said she went into the execution chamber, prepared to die in peace, but instead woke
up confused in a hospital bed.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Early voting numbers this year surpass the total early voting from the 2022 midterms
Michigan U.S. Senate race is a toss-up between Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers
Trump changes schedule to rally Republicans in Selena, Kansas and Dubuque, Iowa
Exxon, Mobil, Chevron, and Shell report soaring quarterly profits amid high fuel prices
China conducts military drills in contested waters near the Philippines after Hegseth's pledge
Tech stock sell-off on Wall Street as AI-driven rally fears grow; S&P 500 drops 1.8%
Christa Pike speaks publicly after surviving failed lethal injection in Tennessee prison
